brought forth no children , but hauing an
handmaid, an Ægyptian named Agar, 2. ſhe
ſaid to her huſband: Behold, our Lord hath

my handrnaid, if happily of her at the leaſt I
may haue children. And when he agreed to her
in this tequeſt, 3. ſhe toke Agar the Ægyptian
her handmaid tenne yeares atter that they firſt
dwelled in the land of Chanaan, and gaue her vnto het huiband to

was with child, detpiſed her mittreſſe. :. And Sarai ſaid to Abram:
Thou doeit vniuſtly againſt me: I gaue my handinaid into thy boſomne,
who perceiuing her ſelf to be with child, deſpiſeth me. Our Lord
iud ge between me and thee. 6. To whom Abram making anſwer :
Behold, ſaith he, thy handmnaid is in thine owne hand, vſe her as it
pleaſeth thee. When Sarai thertore did affflict her, ſhe ranne away.
7. And an Angel of our Lord hauing tound her beſide a fountaine ot
water in the wilderneſſe, which is in the way to Sur in the deſert, d. he
ſaid to her : Agar, the handmaid ot Sarai, whence commeſt thou?
and whither goeſt thou: who anſwered : From the face of Sarai my
miſtreſfe doe I flve. 0. And the Angel of our Lord ſaid to her: Returne
to thy miſtreſſe, and huinble thy ſelte vnder her hand. 10. And againe:
Multiply ing , ſayth he, wil I multiplie thy ſeed , and it ſhal not be num-
bred tor the multitude therot. 11. And againe atter that : Behold, ſaith
he, thou art with child, and thou ſhalt bring forth a ſonne: and thou
ſhalt cal his name Iſinaol, becauſe the Lord hath heard thine atfliction.
12. He ſhal be a wild man: his hand ſhal be againſt al men, and al
mens hands againſt him: and ouer againit al his brethren ſhal he pitch
his tents. 12. And ine called the name ot our Lord that ſpake vnto her :
Thou the God which haſt ſeen me. For ihe ſaid: verily here haue I ſeen
the backe parts ot him that hath ſeen me. 14. Therfote ſhe called that
wel, the wel ot himn that liueth and ſeeth me. The ſame is between
Cadeſſe and Barad. 15. And Agar brought torth a ſonne to Abram :
who called his name Iſmael. 10. Eightie and ſixe yeares old was Abram
when Agar brought him forth Iſmatl.
